transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood AE), Rafael Gomez (Redwood SE), Karen Li (CTO, Lakeshore), Michael Turner (Head of Compliance), Sanjay Patel (Platform Engineer)

Summary: Customer evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private focused on data residency and compliance needs (GDPR, HIPAA-ish concerns for certain lines of business, financial regs, audit logs). Key asks: ensure PII never leaves EU region for specific workloads, explicit log redaction/retention controls, SSO/SAML and RBAC integration, KMS-backed encryption with customer-managed keys, and clarity on audit artifact availability. They want a pilot in our EU region and a technical deep dive to validate network egress and on-prem connectivity.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 45-ish minutes, um, to do an initial discovery, uh, to understand the residency and compliance needs for the LCB use-cases. Rafael is our SE, he'll help with infra details.
[00:17] Karen: thanks Maya, yes appreciate it. we have a few lines of business, but today it's mainly about whether we can use hosted or we need dedicated/private given GDPR and some contractual restrictions with partners.
[00:32] Rafael: cool, quick q \u0005 are you currently running anything LLM-based in prod or mostly proofs right now?
[00:38] Karen: mostly proofs, a vendor POC for client summarization, but it's all in early stage. our core banking and payment flows are on-prem, and we have data classification that says some data is restricted to EU-only processing.
[00:52] Michael: and from compliance perspective, we need to ensure logs, transcripts, and any persisted tokens are kept in-region when the data is marked restricted. also we need an audit trail for who accessed model outputs; retention policies are strict \u0005 could be 3 to 7 years depending on the asset.
[01:10] Maya: understood. we support three deployment modes \u0005 Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC / on-prem). Hosted can be configured for region-specific processing, but you raised the key question: can logs or telemetry leak to other regions or to US-based control plane? Rafael, want to take that?
[01:28] Rafael: yeah, so for Redwood Hosted we offer regional processing in our EU region and we can configure data residency, but there's a control plane that may be multi-region for orchestrations; we can provide contractual commitments in enterprise plans. for stricter needs, Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and dedicated tenancy, and Private gives customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:47] Karen: when you say control plane multi-region, does that mean metadata or logs might be visible outside EU? sponsors of our contracts will push back on any metadata leaving region.
[01:58] Rafael: good point \u0005 metadata control is nuanced. we can map which telemetry is sent to control plane (health checks, metrics). for strict legal requirements, we recommend Private with a customer-managed control plane or Dedicated with contractual guarantees and hosted in EU-only tenancy. we also have options to redact or avoid storing transcripts; but there's trade-offs for debugging and observability.
[02:20] Michael: redact how \u0005 like remove PII at ingestion? we have PII detectors but we need end-to-end proof. also KMS, HSM \u0005 do you integrate with our KMS? we use Azure Key Vault and often use customer-managed keys.
[02:34] Maya: yes, we have KMS integrations \u0005 AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and options for HSM. for Private we can do customer-managed keys and no key material leaves your environment. we'll send our KMS integration notes.
[02:45] Sanjay: latency is also a concern \u0005 core-banking workflows are latency sensitive; if we go Private in our EU datacenter, what's typical p95 for a 512-token prompt? and how much overhead for VPC routing?
[02:58] Rafael: p95 varies but for Dedicated in EU we aim for sub-250ms for short prompts; for 512 tokens, it'll obviously be longer per token. Private on-prem will be similar once provisioned but depends on hardware \u0005 we can size GPUs to meet throughput SLAs. we'll need your traffic profile to right-size.
[03:15] Karen: okay \u0005 also about logs: our security policy forbids storing raw transcripts anywhere except our secure archive; we need to ensure Redwood can either never persist them or push them to our retention store. is that possible?
[03:29] Maya: yes, we have options \u0005 redact at ingress, disable transcript storage, or forward logs directly to your log sink (we support syslog/s3-like sinks in EU). need to confirm specifics for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[03:45] Michael: and HIPAA \u0005 one BU has telehealth partners, so we need HIPAA assurances, BAAs, and strong access controls, plus audit logs. do you have BAAs for Hosted?
[03:57] Rafael: we do offer HIPAA-compliant configurations and can sign BAAs on enterprise plans. typically that pushes customers to Dedicated or Private because of the stricter controls and contractual SLAs.
[04:12] Maya: i'll include the HIPAA + BAA process doc in the pack.
[04:18] [Speaker 1]: um, question on model versions and training \u0005 do you retain prompts or fine-tuning data?
[04:27] Rafael: we don't use customer prompts to train our models by default; when we do offering that, it's opt-in and explicitly declared. for Hosted, we store minimal telemetry unless you opt-in; Dedicated/Private gives more control.
[04:41] Karen: good. what about redaction accuracy? PII detectors are never perfect.
[04:47] Maya: agreed, they're not perfect. we recommend a combination: client-side PII scrubbing + server-side redaction and strict retention policies. we'll include recommended patterns.
[04:58] [00:05:00] Rafael: can you share your list of sensitive data classes and retention windows? that'll help us map product features to your controls.
[05:07] Michael: yes, we'll share the matrix. most sensitive: payment card data, national IDs, account numbers, and some biometric-related stuff. retention mostly 3-7 years per record type.
[05:22] Maya: perfect, we'll align that with our logging/retention options.
[05:30] Karen: interested in how you do access control \u0005 SSO, RBAC, per-route perms? we need separation of duties for dev/test/prod.
[05:38] Rafael: we support SAML/SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC that can be scoped by route, model, or environment. Private gives full control; Dedicated allows role separation via isolated tenants.
[05:50] Sanjay: what's the observability artifact availability? we need immutable audit logs to feed SIEM for 7 years \u0005 can we pull raw audit into our Splunk instance in EU?
[06:02] Maya: yes, we support log forwarding to customer SIEMs and can provide signed audit artifacts. for Hosted we can forward logs; for Dedicated/Private you get more direct access and longer retention options as an add-on.
[06:17] [00:10:00] Karen: someone on legal asked about subprocessors and data transfer \u0005 does Redwood use any third-party subprocessors that might be US-based?
[06:26] Rafael: we do use cloud providers in certain regions, but for EU-only deployments we can limit subprocessors and disclose the list in the DPA. we'll attach the subprocessor list.
[06:36] Michael: we need proof \u0005 SOC2 report, ISO, penetration test summary, encryption certs.
[06:43] Maya: definitely \u0005 i'll include SOC 2 Type II, ISO summary, recent pentest executive summary, and our GDPR DPA template.
[06:52] Karen: what about transcripts that contain PII \u0005 if forwarded to your support team for troubleshooting, how is it handled? we need strict controls.
[07:02] Rafael: support access is audit-logged and restricted; for sensitive customers we can set policies that require ticket-based retrieval and redaction prior to support viewing, or complete avoidance by pushing data to your support-only bucket.
[07:15] Sanjay: on networking \u0005 do you support private link / direct connect to avoid internet egress?
[07:22] Rafael: yes, we support PrivateLink/Direct Connect or equivalent peering in major clouds for Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted can also be fronted by a private connection depending on plan.
[07:33] [00:15:00] Maya: just to summarize the rough recommendations here \u0005 for strict EU-only residency + HIPAA/financial contracts, Private or Dedicated is the safer route, Hosted might be possible with contractual DPA and controls but has more complexity for metadata and telemetry. next steps will be security pack + SE deep dive + pricing/pilot proposal.
[07:51] Karen: that matches our expectation. one more question \u0005 do you provide ability to not store KV cache or to have it ephemeral only? some of our flows store sensitive short-term context.
[07:59] Rafael: yes, we have options to keep KV cache in-memory only and not persist it to disk, or to persist to a customer-managed store in your VPC. spelling in the logs sometimes writes as KV cash in earlier notes, yes.
[08:12] Michael: and can you separate logs by tenant \u0005 we have multi-tenant customers, need per-tenant isolation for logs and outputs.
[08:20] Rafael: we support per-tenant isolation and logical separation; Dedicated gives you stronger tenancy guarantees.
[08:29] [00:20:00] Karen: sample legal language \u0005 can you commit to EU-only processing for restricted data and provide export controls?
[08:38] Maya: we can include EU-only processing clauses in the DPA for specific data classes and can flag which deployment mode requires Private vs Dedicated. we'll have legal propose language.
[08:47] Sanjay: for the pilot, we'll want to test with a redacted subset of production data and run throughput tests \u0005 can Redwood provide a pilot environment in our EU region for 4 weeks?
[08:57] Rafael: yes, we typically run 2-6 week pilots; for Dedicated/Private we can provision trial capacity, and for Hosted we can do a region-limited sandbox. we'll size based on your traffic profile.
[09:10] Michael: cost \u0005 Dedicated seems expensive, but if it's the only way to meet compliance we need numbers. please show cost-per-conversation and options for burst capacity.
[09:20] Maya: will include cost examples and the Optimize levers (batching, quantization) to reduce unit cost.
[09:28] [00:30:00] Karen: any known limitations around embedded PII removal and e2e encryption? we want assurance that even internal logs are encrypted and keys managed by us.
[09:38] Rafael: e2e is possible in Private; key-escrow patterns and HSM are an option. for Hosted, customer-managed keys in Azure/AWS are supported but some meta-ops may still be handled by Redwood. we'll outline the residual metadata footprint.
[09:53] Maya: this is where we usually show the architecture doc, i'll attach in follow-up: https://docs.redwood.ai/security (link), and also the EU deployment checklist: https://docs.redwood.ai/eu-deploy-checklist.
[10:05] Karen: perfect. one small failure we saw in a PoC with a different vendor was that automatic transcripts got stored in a US S3 bucket even though processing was EU \u0005 we need a guarantee it won't happen.
[10:17] Rafael: understood, we'll show an evidence matrix of where different artifacts are stored and options to forward artifacts to your buckets.
[10:24] Maya: ok, last set of things \u0005 who is the decision org and timeline?
[10:29] Karen: decision committee includes CTO, Head of Compliance, and Procurement; target decision window is Q1 2027 but we want a pilot before EOY to validate.
[10:39] Michael: approvals depend heavily on legal sign-off of DPA and subprocessor list.
[10:44] Maya: understo od. we'll prioritize the security pack and the SE deep dive.
[10:49] [00:40:00] Rafael: any specific endpoints or integrations we should cover in the deep dive?
[10:55] Sanjay: SAML, Azure Key Vault, direct connect, and log-forwarding to our Splunk instance in EU. also we want an example Terraform module for Private deployment.
[11:06] Rafael: got it \u0005 we'll prepare an infra sketch and sample terraform references.
[11:12] Karen: great. that's all from me. thanks.
[11:16] Maya: thanks everyone \u0005 we'll follow up with the pack and scheduling links.

Action items (as mentioned):
- Maya: send SOC2, pentest summary, GDPR DPA, HIPAA+BAA docs, EU deployment checklist and pricing - by 2026-11-20
- Rafael: prepare technical architecture for Private VPC and Direct Connect, include KMS/HSM notes - by 2026-11-24
- Michael: provide data classification and retention windows, confirm decision timeline - by 2026-11-24
- Sanjay: share traffic profile and latency targets - by 2026-11-23

References/Shared docs:
- Security pack (SOC2, ISO, pentest): https://docs.redwood.ai/security
- EU deploy checklist: https://docs.redwood.ai/eu-deploy-checklist
- Pilot request form (internal link): https://app.redwood.ai/pilot-request

End of transcript.
